content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Summary:** The APCN 2 Agreement has no governing-law or court-venue provision. Paragraph 27.2 does the opposite — it instructs that indicia of any particular national law be disregarded — and Paragraph 27.1 makes Management Committee referral (which may itself "determine the method, such as arbitration") the "sole and exclusive remedy," with Paragraph 20 contemplating arbitration outside a Party's own country. That fails both the preferred and fallback checklists and sits close to walk-away territory (committee-imposed, potentially foreign arbitration with no court forum).

**Redline (preferred level, ok:true):**
1. Paragraph 27.1 — removed the arbitration-election and "sole and exclusive remedy" language, routing unresolved disputes to Paragraph 27.2 so the escalation step is preserved but no longer displaces the courts.
2. Paragraph 27.2 — replaced the anti-choice-of-law sentence with New York governing law plus exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, reserving only temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.

Both preferred elements are mapped; Delaware, California, or England and Wales with the courts of London is offered as a fallback in the comment.
